sources.entry: zoneinfo - (Python standard library) IANA time zone support. Brings the tz database into Python.

summary.name: tz database
summary.one_liner: The tz database (also called tzdata, zoneinfo, or the IANA time zone database) is a public-domain collaborative compilation of world time zone rules and daylight saving time history used by computer systems.
use_cases: Converting times between time zones in software
Looking up historical daylight saving time rules
Providing time zone data to operating systems and programming languages
Choosing correct IANA timezone names for applications
Keeping time zone data updated on servers and devices
summary.what_it_does: The database lists time zones as Area/Location names such as America/New_York and records their offsets from UTC, daylight saving time rules and historical changes since 1970. The text source files are compiled by the zic tool into binary files, one per timezone, which operating systems and libraries read. The reference code includes readers for standard APIs like localtime() and mktime(). New editions are published several times per year as changes warrant. The page also notes it does not include geographic boundary coordinates, which are published separately by a third party.
notable: Public-domain data and reference code maintained by Paul Eggert, with ICANN oversight since 2011
Uniform Area/Location naming convention used by many programming languages and databases
Compiled to platform-independent binary files by the zic compiler
Used by Python zoneinfo, Go time, Java java.time, PostgreSQL, and many other systems
caveats: Changes to time zone rules can take time to reach end users because software must update its copy of the database
Pre-1970 data is not guaranteed correct for the whole region represented by a zone name
A 2011 copyright lawsuit led to temporary shutdown of the mailing list and FTP site before it was dismissed in 2012
